plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value ($22) maximizes my expected profit - I won't overpay since I only pay what the second-highest bidder bid, and I won't underbid and risk losing a profitable opportunity. This is theoretically optimal in this auction format.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid here, unlike first-price auctions. Thus, I will bid my true value of $34 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily, while bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth. With no prior history to adjust for, I'll bid my true value of $10 to maximize expected profit.
